facts.statement: Erpetosuchus lived during the Late Triassic period.
Erpetosuchus was first described by E. T. Newton in 1894 based on remains found in northeastern Scotland.
facts.quote: It was first described by E. T. Newton in 1894 for remains found in northeastern Scotland

facts.statement: The original description included four specimens from the latest Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone Formation.
facts.quote: including four specimens from the latest Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone Formation

facts.statement: Additional remains of Erpetosuchus have been found in the New Haven Formation of Connecticut in the eastern United States.
facts.quote: Additional remains of Erpetosuchus have been found in the New Haven Formation of Connecticut in the eastern United States

facts.statement: American paleontologist Paul E. Olsen discovered a partial skull of Erpetosuchus in 1995 during a field trip in Connecticut.
facts.quote: During a field trip in 1995 to the lower part of the New Haven Formation in Connecticut, American palaeontologist Paul E. Olsen discovered a partial skull

facts.statement: The Connecticut skull was the first record of Erpetosuchus found outside Scotland.
facts.quote: This was the first record of Erpetosuchus outside Scotland

facts.statement: The New Haven Formation where the Connecticut specimen was found dates to the Norian age.
facts.quote: Dating of the lower portion of the New Haven Formation indicates a Norian age

facts.statement: Erpetosuchus granti was originally assigned to Thecodontia, but this classification is now considered invalid.
facts.quote: Erpetosuchus granti was originally assigned to Thecodontia, but that name is no longer considered valid in scientific literature because it is a paraphyletic group of early archosaurs

facts.statement: An analysis by Olsen et al. in 2000 suggested Erpetosuchus granti is the sister-taxon to Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: A more recent phylogenetic analysis by Olsen et al. (2000) found E. granti to be the sister-taxon to the Crocodylomorpha

facts.statement: It is debated whether Erpetosuchus is closely related to Crocodylomorpha, as some analyses suggest an unresolved relationship at the base of Archosauria instead.
facts.quote: Nesbitt and Butler did not find support for the sister-group relationship between Erpetosuchus and Crocodylomorpha. Instead, erpetosuchids formed a polytomy or unresolved evolutionary relationship at the base of Archosauria along with several other groups

facts.statement: Erpetosuchus is classified within the unranked family Paracrocodylomorpha.
Erpetosuchus belongs to the family Erpetosuchidae.
Erpetosuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
